notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2023, as the county reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
The Census surveys every government only in Census of Governments years (2022) and a sample in other years, so FY 2023 is the latest available.
Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Payments to other governments ($72,000) are left out, because the government receiving them reports that spending.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.
Political money is not scored: contributions to North Dakota county candidates were not loaded.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-18. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals, corporate tax breaks and license-plate cameras mapped by volunteers have not been checked for North Dakota yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: Face recognition
redFlags.detail: The Burleigh County Sheriff's Department can run face recognition requests through the North Dakota Bureau of Criminal Investigation's face recognition system. The agency submitted five requests through the Bureau of Criminal Investigation's face recognition system between March 2023 to October 2024.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS012159, citing Bureau Of Criminal Investigation Division of North Dakota

redFlags.label: Face recognition
redFlags.detail: The Burleigh County State's Attorney's Office can run face recognition requests through the North Dakota Bureau of Criminal Investigation's face recognition system. The agency submitted two requests through the Bureau of Criminal Investigation's face recognition system between March 2023 to October 2024.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS012160, citing Bureau Of Criminal Investigation Division of North Dakota

redFlags.label: Police drones
redFlags.detail: The Burleigh County Sheriff's Office operates five DJI drones as of 2016, according to data compiled by the Center for the Study of the Drone at Bard College.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS003087, citing Center for the Study of the Drone at Bard College

notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024, as the city reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included. Residents also pay Burleigh County.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Payments to other governments ($127,000) are left out, because the government receiving them reports that spending.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.
Political money is not scored: contributions to North Dakota local candidates were not loaded.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Cameras: 139 license-plate cameras are mapped inside City of Bismarck's borders in OpenStreetMap (5 made by Flock Safety), not counting cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies. Flock cameras count as a red flag whoever runs them. Other brands count only when the government is the recorded operator, since many have no operator recorded.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-18. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals and corporate tax breaks have not been checked for North Dakota yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: Flock camera network
redFlags.detail: 5 Flock Safety license-plate cameras are mapped inside City of Bismarck's borders in OpenStreetMap. Flock cameras photograph every passing car and feed a search network shared with police agencies across the country. Who runs each camera is not recorded; cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies are not counted.

source.label: OpenStreetMap license-plate cameras (as mapped by DeFlock)
